clue.text: Marked "articulated"

blocks.note: first meaning: very noticeable, conspicuous
second meaning: spoken aloud clearly

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a label stuck on a word; the two words are separate senses of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strongly noticeable, as in a strong accent, and uttered or sounded out in speech.

clue.text: High position for leading hand in pigskin manufacture

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is the one at its front
manufacture means making something new out of raw material, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the first letter of hand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior post goes to the most skilled worker in a leather goods factory making pigskin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading hand' reads as a foreman, but it only supplies the opening letter of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a monarch is the loftiest rank in a realm, so royal status counts as an elevated station.

clue.text: Business intrigue

blocks.note: first meaning: a matter or concern
second meaning: a secret love liaison

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about corporate scheming; the words are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a matter to deal with, as in foreign affairs, and also an illicit romantic liaison.

clue.text: Reject some timid or pusillanimous thrust

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, so the letters sit inside them
to reject is to throw back, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of timid, all of or, and the start of pusillanimous

explanation.surface: Turn down a feeble, cowardly push, as though dismissing a weak attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A poke or jab with a finger or stick is a short sharp push forward.

clue.text: With nice discrimination of French artist, including a version of Act 1

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so the letters come out in a different order
including means taking something inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the French word for of
Sir Peter Lely, the Dutch-born portrait painter at the court of Charles II
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A refined critique of a French painter's take on the opening act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Lely is a favourite crossword painter. The shuffled letters go inside him, after the French word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice here has its old sense of fine or precise, so discriminating finely means acting with tact and subtle care.

clue.text: Thought table to be one of no practical use

blocks.note: a thought is a notion
a table is a tabulated list

explanation.surface: A philosopher dismisses a piece of furniture as useless, the way an abstract thinker might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thought table' looks like a single object, but it splits into two nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guided by lofty principles rather than realism is often dismissed as an impractical dreamer.

clue.text: Minister needing to look into the future

blocks.note: first meaning: a clergyman or theologian
second meaning: to foretell or guess by intuition

explanation.surface: A churchman is required to make prophecies.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is an old term for a cleric; as a verb it means to discover by insight or prophecy.

clue.text: Incline to be on the skinny side

blocks.note: first meaning: to tilt or slope
second meaning: thin, with little fat

explanation.surface: Someone tends toward being rather thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for tilting from the upright and an adjective for slim or free of fat.

clue.text: Strengthen check on police, perhaps

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
the police are an example of a force

explanation.surface: Tighten up oversight of the constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks police as one example of the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster a structure or an army is to give it added support, making it sturdier.

clue.text: Run-producing stroke

blocks.note: surface reading: a shot that scores, in cricket
setter's reading: also hints at running a vehicle or a machine, a stroke of an engine

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman's forward attacking shot along the ground often yields runs; the word also means to run a car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a powerful forward batting shot in cricket or golf, struck to send the ball far.

clue.text: Drink round drawback to one unwilling to spend

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way

blocks.note: a spirit
read as draw back: draw is drag, as on a cigarette, and back turns it the other way

explanation.surface: Buying a round is the downside of drinking for a skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one noun, but it splits into a verb and an instruction to turn it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a stingy, miserly person who hoards money and hates paying out.

clue.text: European may object to a reverse fastener

indicators.note: reverse means put in the opposite direction, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: it is a pronoun for an object
taken as written
a nail fastens things together

explanation.surface: A continental might protest about a zip or button put on back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb meaning protest; it is the noun, giving the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Italy is a citizen of a country on that continent.

clue.text: Old teacher lady in ancient city

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: Ur of the Chaldees, the Mesopotamian city
the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A former schoolmistress living in some antique city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's standard ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly this was the title of an assistant master or under-teacher in a British school.

clue.text: Characteristic of fleshy part of head after a time, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words might be arranged some other way

blocks.note: taken as written
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: Something typical of a plump part of the skull after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a promontory, as in Dungeness, so head here means a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshiness or substance is the quality of the soft muscular tissue, so the word names that trait.

clue.text: Masculine component in transgressor

blocks.note: a synonym
a factor is a contributing element

explanation.surface: The male element is a big part of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal term for a criminal or wrongdoer who breaks the law.

clue.text: Shows at which glasses are required?

blocks.note: first meaning: grand public displays or performances
second meaning: a pair of lenses worn to correct eyesight

explanation.surface: Performances where the audience must wear eyewear, like 3D films, or where drinks flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the two nouns share one word rather than the clue describing a single event.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means grand displays or performances and is also the formal name for a pair of eyeglasses.

clue.text: Splendid bit of writing with unhappy ending

definitions.text: Splendid bit of writing with unhappy ending

blocks.note: capital is old British slang for excellent
a sentence is a unit of prose
no letters: it turns the whole clue into a description of a death penalty

explanation.surface: A fine passage of prose that closes on a sad note.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words build the answer, and the whole clue then defines it: a court's judgement whose ending is the condemned person's death.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a court order condemning someone to death, the most severe punishment the law can impose.

clue.text: Clothing employers give up scrap first

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters climb, so they read backwards
first puts the turned piece at the front, before the other piece

blocks.note: an ort is a scrap of leftover food
people who employ something use it

explanation.surface: Bosses abandon a squabble over the dress code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight; it is the crossword's favourite leftover morsel, ORT.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a garment for the legs, so the word is an example of things people wear.

clue.text: Futile to turn weapon on a politician

indicators.note: to turn the word is to make it face the other way

blocks.note: a firearm
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: It is pointless to aim a gun at an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' places the turned weapon above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trifling, worthless or ineffective, so something of this kind achieves nothing.

clue.text: Insect acting as brake on vehicle

blocks.note: a drag is something that slows motion
taken as written
a fly is an old one-horse hired carriage

explanation.surface: A bug serving to slow down a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly was a light horse-drawn cab in Victorian Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-bodied, fast-flying winged creature with large eyes, a member of that class of creatures.

clue.text: Cast down when discovered in a plot

indicators.note: to be discovered in something is to be found inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a garden plot is a flower bed
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Depressed on being found out in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a conspiracy; here it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbled or degraded in rank or esteem, someone has been brought low, lowered in status.

clue.text: Sound ceremonial observance for Conservatives

indicators.note: sound tells us we hear the word spoken, not see it spelt

blocks.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

explanation.surface: A traditional ritual that appeals to Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective for the ceremony; it signals a word heard, not read.
explanation.definitionFit: The political right wing is the collective name for the conservative parties and their supporters.

clue.text: Cause for debate

blocks.note: first meaning: a ground or motive
second meaning: to argue logically

explanation.surface: Grounds for an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a motive or ground; as a verb it means to argue or think things through logically.

clue.text: Girl appearing in first part of Cicero, or any great writer

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening few letters
appearing in something means showing up inside it

blocks.note: the opening three letters of the Roman orator's name
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman features in the opening of a Roman orator's work, or some other master author.
explanation.walkthrough: Cicero is himself a fine example of the answer, which makes the definition neat.
explanation.definitionFit: An author whose works are recognised as of lasting excellence, especially of Greek or Latin antiquity, is called this.

clue.text: Turn up in a small boat

blocks.note: first meaning: to tilt upward, as an ear or a hat brim
second meaning: a cockboat, a ship's small rowing boat

explanation.surface: Arrive aboard a dinghy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive'; it means to tilt upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog cocks its ear by raising it, and the noun is an old word for a light rowing boat or dinghy.

clue.text: Mad at French trick

blocks.note: the abbreviation for French
an antic is a prank or caper

explanation.surface: Angry about a Gallic ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild with fear or worry, someone in this state behaves in a frenzied, desperate way.

clue.text: Instrument found in central Scotland

definitions.note: a region named by its place, not a phrase of the same part of speech

blocks.note: first meaning: a small high-pitched flute
second meaning: a Scottish council area and old kingdom north of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A musical instrument native to the Scottish heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bagpipes; the instrument's name is also a region of Scotland, the peninsula between the Firths of Forth and Tay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small military flute and also a Scottish county lying in the east of the country's central belt.

clue.text: Shout of welcome for revolutionary monarch

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Cuban revolutionary
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A crowd hails a rebel king.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurrah or cry of approval is how crowds greet arriving people they applaud.

clue.text: Adrift certainly about a foot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: of course means certainly
F is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Drifting, surely, by around twelve inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase of course opens up after its first word to take the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is adrift has wandered from its planned route, straying from its heading.
